title: Intelligence Briefing Dashboard
subtitle: Weekly Conflict Monitor · All Regions
sources: Reuters · AP News · Al Jazeera · ACLED · US Embassy Alerts · LiveUAMap · BNO News · ISW · British Defence Intelligence · Kyiv Post · Sudan Tribune · Irrawaddy · CNN · NBC · CBS · Fox News · HRW · UN News · CFR · Times of Israel · NPR · CNBC · Atlantic Council · Sudan Tribune · US State Dept · OHCHR · Wikipedia · Washington Post · Amnesty International · AEI · Moscow Times · Kyiv Independent

regions.name: Middle East
overview: The Iran ceasefire has collapsed and the war has widened onto two new fronts in a single week — the 25-27 Jul pause broke on 29-30 Jul with Iranian strikes on Jordan and Iraq-based US forces, triggering a US 'heavy wave' of strikes on southern Iran and a joint US-Saudi combat operation against Iran-backed militias inside Iraq, the most significant expansion of the conflict since it began.

Egypt has been drawn directly into the war for the first time — a 29 Jul drone strike on US-owned LNG shipping at Damietta port, unclaimed but assessed as deliberate, breaks Cairo's prior insulation from the conflict and compounds economic strain from the 15 Jul Suez surcharge hikes.

The Gulf oil-war threshold crossed in late July is being actively sustained, not resolved — continuing Houthi tanker strikes (22, 28 Jul) and a declared blockade of Saudi Arabia, layered on the 25 Jul Aramco refinery strikes, are keeping Brent above $100/barrel and have prompted a 14-nation Saudi-led 'Maritime Defense Alliance' proposal.

Israel is now managing simultaneous escalations on three fronts — near-daily Lebanon drone strikes and continued Gaza ceasefire-violation deaths persist alongside an unprecedented West Bank spiral, where the 24 Jul al-Tal killings triggered a formal 'wide-scale military operation' and settler reprisals the UN says have pushed settler violence to an all-time high.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 17 Jul — Gaza Strip: Israeli attacks killed 14 Palestinians, more than half of them mourners struck by a drone during a funeral procession.
26 Jul — Deir al-Balah: An Israeli air strike killed two Hamas security officials, including the head of Hamas's internal security service, when their vehicle was hit.
30 Jul — Gaza-wide: Fresh Israeli strikes killed at least four to six people, including children, across the Strip.
30 Jul — Gaza-wide: The cumulative death toll since the October 2025 ceasefire reached at least 1,207 Palestinians killed, with Israel expanding physical control over more than half the enclave.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Strike tempo remains the highest since the ceasefire began, with the cumulative toll continuing to climb and Israel entrenching behind an expanded physical barrier over more than half the enclave. Expect continued near-daily strikes under a nominally intact truce, punctuated by multi-fatality incidents (funerals, official convoys) that sustain international condemnation without a formal collapse. Watch for Gaza operations to be used as a pressure valve or bandwidth drain as the wider Iran-Israel war intensifies.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 10 Jul — Kfarrumman, Nabatieh district: Israeli drone strikes on a motorcycle and car killed one and wounded three.
28 Jul — Nabatieh al-Fawqa: Israeli drones struck an apartment complex, causing substantial damage and fire.
30 Jul — Southern Lebanon/Beirut: Israeli forces intensified overnight operations with drone strikes and explosive demolitions in several towns; drones also overflew Beirut and its southern suburbs.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The US-brokered withdrawal framework remains functionally inoperative as a restraint on Israeli strikes, which continue near-daily in the Nabatieh corridor. Israeli overflights of Beirut itself signal willingness to project pressure beyond the south, raising the risk of a strike inside greater Beirut within the 90-day window. Sustained attrition raises pressure for a Hezbollah retaliatory incident, particularly if it coincides with a widening Iran-US war drawing in Lebanese Shia armed factions.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 25-27 Jul — Nationwide: A fragile pause held as Trump said the US halted strikes at Tehran's request pending a new ceasefire deal, while Iran denied it was engaged in talks.
29-30 Jul — Jordan/Iraq: Iran launched renewed missile and drone attacks on US forces in Jordan and on positions tied to the wider conflict, breaking the pause.

30 Jul — Qeshm Island/Ahvaz/Abadan: The US conducted a 'heavy wave' of strikes on dozens of IRGC targets across southern Iran; a couple and their two-year-old child were killed in a residential building on Qeshm.
30 Jul — Washington: The US Senate killed a Democrat-backed Iran War Powers resolution 49-50, the 13th such vote of the war.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained; the brief pause proved a tactical lull, not a durable ceasefire. Expect continued strike-counterstrike cycles between the US and Iran, with Iran increasingly using proxy and direct strikes against third countries (Jordan, Iraq, now Egypt) to raise costs on Washington without a homeland-to-homeland breakthrough. Congressional efforts to constrain the administration have repeatedly failed, removing a near-term domestic check. Absent a Qatar/Pakistan-brokered breakthrough, expect the war to grind on past the 90-day horizon with periodic pauses followed by renewed heavy strike waves and growing regional spillover.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 20 Jul — Nationwide: Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, accusing Riyadh of imposing an 'unjust and oppressive siege' on Yemen.

25 Jul — Jizan/Yanbu, Saudi Arabia: Houthis struck Aramco refineries with ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones — their first direct hit on Saudi oil infrastructure since 2022; Jizan's 400,000-bpd refinery shut down, restart not expected until mid-August.
28 Jul — Red Sea: Houthis fired missiles at another Saudi oil tanker, enforcing the blockade.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Houthis have moved from harassment to sustained blockade enforcement against Saudi-linked shipping, with the Jizan and Yanbu strikes marking a qualitative escalation. Expect continued tanker strikes and possible additional refinery/export-infrastructure attacks as long as Saudi strikes on Hodeidah continue, sustaining Brent crude above $100/barrel. Watch for a full Saudi counter-offensive against Houthi positions and for the newly proposed 14-nation Maritime Defense Alliance to formalize an international naval response.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 24 Jul — Al-Tal village, near Nablus: A settler attack on Palestinian homes triggered a shootout that killed 4 Palestinians and 2 Israelis, the deadliest single settler-related incident of the current wave.
26-27 Jul — West Bank-wide: Netanyahu ordered a 'wide-scale military operation' across the West Bank; IDF stormed multiple towns as settler violence intensified in reprisal.
27 Jul — West Bank: UN OCHA data showed 3,033 recorded Israeli settler attacks between Jan 2025 and June 2026, with the UN warning settler violence has hit an 'all-time high.'
30 Jul — West Bank: Escalation continued with a surge in IDF checkpoints alongside ongoing settler violence.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The 24 Jul al-Tal killings have catalyzed the sharpest West Bank escalation since 2022, now compounded by a formal IDF 'wide-scale operation.' Expect continued settler reprisal attacks, expanded checkpoints, and elevated risk of further fatal clashes. HRW's mass-atrocity warning and the UN's 'all-time high' characterization suggest international pressure will intensify, but with no de-escalation signal from Israeli authorities the trajectory points toward continued deterioration, particularly as the West Bank becomes a secondary front while security attention is absorbed by Gaza, Lebanon and the Iran war.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 15 Jul — Erbil: Six drones targeted Erbil International Airport and the US Consulate; all intercepted by air defenses.
26 Jul — Erbil: A further drone attack was reported, with explosions near a US base close to Erbil airport.

29-30 Jul — Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala, Diyala: US and Saudi forces conducted joint precision strikes on Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces sites, including PMF's Baghdad HQ, following 30+ militia drone attacks on US assets over 72 hours; strikes killed roughly 20 militia fighters and 6 Iranian advisers.
30 Jul — Nationwide: Militia leadership signaled intent to retaliate within 72 hours, reportedly considering targets in Iraqi Kurdistan or Baghdad.
countries.coa: Upgraded to CRITICAL from HIGH. Iraq has become an active US-Saudi combat theater against Iran-backed militias, with confirmed fatalities on both sides and an open militia threat of imminent retaliation — a material escalation beyond last week's intercepted-drone-attack posture. Expect an escalatory tit-for-tat: further militia drone/rocket attacks on US and Saudi-linked targets met with continued US-Saudi strikes on PMF-aligned factions. Baghdad's ability to restrain Iran-aligned militias will likely erode further, raising risk of the 30 Sep Kataib Hezbollah disarmament deadline collapsing into open confrontation.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 25 Jul — Jizan/Yanbu: Houthi ballistic missile and drone strikes damaged Aramco's Jizan refinery (shut down, fire ongoing) and Yanbu storage facilities; Yanbu loading volumes fell roughly 40% since 19 Jul.
22 & 28 Jul — Red Sea: Two additional Houthi tanker attacks tied to the declared blockade.

29-30 Jul — Iraq: Saudi Arabia joined US forces in direct strikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq, killing 20 fighters and 6 Iranian advisers — a significant expansion of Saudi military involvement beyond its own borders.
30 Jul — Nationwide: Saudi Arabia proposed a 'Maritime Defense Alliance,' now backed by 14 countries, to protect regional shipping routes.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Saudi Arabia has moved from a defensive posture to active co-belligerency, now conducting offensive strikes inside Iraq alongside the US. Expect continued Aramco infrastructure vulnerability — the targeted mid-August Jizan restart is itself an attack-window risk — sustained tanker harassment, and a push to operationalize the Maritime Defense Alliance within the 90-day window. Riyadh's deepening direct military role raises the risk of further Houthi/Iranian retaliation against Saudi territory beyond Jizan/Yanbu.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: Jul (ongoing) — Aleppo/Azaz/Al-Bab: Syria's Interior Ministry announced the arrest of seven suspected ISIS-cell members in a joint operation targeting cells in Aleppo city and surrounding towns.
Jul (ongoing) — Aleppo/Al-Bab: Follow-on raids saw authorities arrest additional suspected Daesh members and seize explosives and weapons.

Through Jul — Nationwide: The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights recorded five ISIS attacks in July alone; total ISIS attacks across Syria in 2026 now stand at 64, evidence the group is actively trying to regroup.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Aleppo front remains the epicenter of ISIL's resurgence, with security services conducting active counter-cell operations even as attack frequency continues to climb year-on-year. Expect continued low-intensity ISIL hit-and-run attacks and periodic counter-terrorism raids in Aleppo, Azaz and Al-Bab. Syria's neutral posture in the Iran-US war remains intact for now, but as the war's geographic footprint widens into Iraq, Jordan and Egypt, the risk of Syrian territory being drawn in continues to rise.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 15 Jul — Suez Canal-wide: The Canal Authority raised transit surcharges for most vessel classes (loaded tankers up to 37%, dry bulk to 22%, containerships 12%).

29 Jul — Damietta port: A drone strike hit the US-owned LNG floating storage vessel Energos Winter, with fire spreading to a second ship, the Gaslog Salem; no casualties, crews evacuated — the first confirmed attack on Egyptian soil since the Iran war began.
countries.coa: Upgraded to HIGH from MODERATE. A direct, if unclaimed, drone strike on Egyptian port infrastructure marks a qualitative break from last week's purely economic profile and pulls Egypt directly into the widening regional war. Expect a heightened security posture around Mediterranean ports and Suez Canal approaches, alongside continued economic pressure from elevated transit surcharges suppressing already-depressed canal volumes. A repeat attack, especially one causing casualties or targeting canal-adjacent infrastructure, would likely force a formal Egyptian military response and materially raise the threat picture further.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 22-23 Jul — Aqaba: Iran launched missiles and drones at Aqaba port and airport; Jordanian forces intercepted six missiles and four drones, with explosions heard over neighboring Eilat.
29-30 Jul — Aqaba: A renewed Iranian strike targeted the port city; Jordan's Foreign Ministry summoned Iran's charge d'affaires and lodged a formal protest over 'continuing, unjustified attacks.'
30 Jul — Nationwide: Air defenses shot down five additional missiles launched from Iran; an Iranian strike separately hit a building belonging to a Chinese firm, killing one person.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Jordan has now been struck by Iran at least twice in nine days, a shift from a single intercepted incident to a repeated targeting pattern. Expect continued Iranian strikes on Jordanian territory as Tehran uses Aqaba to pressure US regional basing and shipping without striking Israel or Gulf states directly, sustaining risk to civilians and infrastructure. Jordan's formal diplomatic protests are unlikely to deter further strikes absent a broader Iran-US de-escalation.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 12 Jul — Gatrun, southern Libya: A newly self-proclaimed rebel group, the 'Southern Liberation Operations Room,' attacked a Libyan National Army checkpoint.
20 Jul — Eastern Libya: Turkey expanded military and technical cooperation with Haftar's LNA, a development Egypt reportedly views with concern.
25 Jul — Tripoli and other cities: Protests erupted over power cuts and heatwave-driven electricity shortages; a civil disobedience campaign shut down roads and public buildings.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Libya's trajectory remains one of political consolidation under Haftar, aided by deepening Turkish engagement, combined with rising civil unrest over basic services. The Gatrun checkpoint attack signals a new, still-marginal armed challenger in the south worth monitoring. Expect continued Tripoli-area protests over power and utilities through the summer heat season, with risk of escalation into clashes with militias if government responses remain inadequate.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 4 Jul — Tunis: A court convicted Ennahda Secretary-General Ajmi Ourimi and party member Mosaab Gharbi, sentencing both to three years.
8 Jul — Tunis: A court sentenced 21 people, including Ennahda leaders and former officials, to 12-35 years; former Ennahda president Rached Ghannouchi received a 14-year sentence in absentia.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The judicial crackdown on Ennahda appears to have reached a steady state following the early-July sentencing wave, with no new arrests or violent incidents identified this week. Expect continued appeals and international human-rights criticism, but no near-term shift toward street-level unrest absent a new triggering event.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: Ukraine's political-military crisis has hardened into stalemate rather than resolving — Drapatyi's appointment as Commander-in-Chief defused some anger, but Fedorov's refusal of any post short of reinstatement kept protests running past two weeks even as the presidential office treats the matter as closed, a rift that could reopen sharply if front-line reverses or further mass-casualty strikes occur.

Russia intensified deep strikes on Kyiv and other cities in the final week of July, while Ukraine matched the escalation with fresh long-range hits on Russian refineries (29 Jul) and repeated drone/naval attacks on Novorossiysk's CPC terminal (20 Jul, 30 Jul), deepening a fuel crisis now affecting roughly two-thirds of Russian regions.

Belarus continues using the Ukraine border as a coercive lever on two tracks simultaneously — Lukashenko-confirmed Special Operations Forces dispersal alongside continued border infrastructure buildup, paired with a sustained migrant-pressure campaign against Latvia now past 111 consecutive days of crossings tied explicitly to Latvia's Ukraine support.

The wider region shows an accelerating east-west fracture that Moscow's traditional levers are struggling to reverse — Georgia's protest movement passed 600+ days with continuing state harassment of journalists and comedians, Armenia absorbed a further Russian trade squeeze, while Moldova's confirmed Tofan government and Azerbaijan's Berlin energy diplomacy both signal deepening Western alignment.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 21 Jul — Kyiv: Zelensky appointed General Mykhailo Drapatyi as new Commander-in-Chief following Syrskyi's dismissal; Fedorov rejected the offer of a technology-sector post on 23 Jul, insisting on nothing short of reinstatement as defense minister.
25 Jul — Nationwide: Protests reached their 10th consecutive day, spreading across Lviv, Ivano-Frankivsk, Uzhhorod, Dnipro and other cities.

25-27 Jul — Kyiv: Russia launched an overnight ballistic missile barrage on a residential building, followed by a further strike of 7 ballistic missiles and 136 drones that killed at least 6 civilians nationwide.
29 Jul — Southern Russia: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on two major Russian oil refineries, terminals and 18 vessels, hours after a Zelensky-Trump meeting.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, compounding. The leadership crisis has hardened into stalemate rather than resolved, running in parallel with intensified Russian strikes on Kyiv and an expanded Ukrainian long-range campaign against Russian refining capacity. Expect the Fedorov standoff to persist as low-boil civil unrest, with Drapatyi's appointment facing its first major test on force-generation and Pokrovsk-axis defense, while Russia sustains mass missile/drone barrages and Ukraine continues to escalate refinery and Black Sea terminal strikes as a countervailing lever.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 20 Jul — Novorossiysk: A drone attack struck a tanker near the CPC terminal, forcing suspension of oil loading.
29 Jul — Southern Russia: Ukraine confirmed strikes on two major refineries and associated terminals, hitting 18 vessels.
30 Jul — Novorossiysk: A UAV strike hit the tanker Nissos Sifnos near CPC crude-receiving manifolds, sparking a fire and again disrupting shipments.
Late Jul — Nationwide: Roughly two-thirds of Russian regions are experiencing fuel shortages; Ukrainian strikes are estimated to have cut Russian oil production/export capacity by roughly 40%.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained, pressure intensifying. Russia's fuel-supply crisis will likely deepen through August as Ukraine continues to prioritize refinery and Black Sea export-terminal strikes, with Novorossiysk/CPC remaining a repeat target given its outsized role in Russian and Kazakh crude exports. Expect further localized states of emergency, expanding regional fuel rationing, and continued mass strikes on Ukrainian cities as an asymmetric counter-pressure tool. Absent a ceasefire, the refinery/tanker exchange looks set to become the primary attrition axis of the war through Q4 2026.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 22 Jul — Belarus-Ukraine border: Lukashenko confirmed he ordered Special Operations Forces dispersed along the border, framing it as defensive, amid continued construction of roads and ammunition/fuel storage sites near the frontier.
1 Jul — Latvia border: Lithuania began sending a 9-officer mission, including 2 K9 handlers, to reinforce Latvia's border guard against Belarus-directed migrant flows.

15 Jul — Latvia border: Latvia logged 111 consecutive days of migrant crossing attempts from Belarus (7,634 this year, roughly 800 more than last year), explicitly linked by officials to Latvia's support for Ukraine.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Belarus will likely continue using both the SOF border dispersal and the migrant-pressure campaign as parallel hybrid levers rather than escalating toward direct military action, with the border infrastructure buildup suggesting sustained readiness rather than imminent offensive intent. Pressure on Latvia is likely to intensify through its October elections, with Baltic states increasing mutual-aid border deployments.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: 21 Jul — Chișinău: Parliament elected businessman Vasile Tofan as prime minister (53-21), backed by President Sandu's PAS party.
22 Jul — Chișinău: The Tofan government was sworn in, naming EU accession its top priority, targeting an accession treaty signed by end-2028 and membership readiness by 2030.
Late Jul — Chișinău: The new government's national security program explicitly named Russia as the primary threat, citing energy leverage, electoral interference, propaganda and cyberattacks.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The Tofan government's technocratic profile will likely be tested quickly on delivery — anti-corruption reform and EU cluster negotiations are the near-term benchmarks. Expect Russia to continue applying pressure through energy leverage, disinformation and possible electoral interference rather than overt escalation, making Chișinău a bellwether for broader enlargement momentum through Q4 2026.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 22 Jul — Tbilisi: Journalist Vako Sanaia was arrested and sentenced to 14 days over statements about the parliament speaker; comedian Onise Okriashvili was beaten near his home the same day.
26 Jul — Tbilisi: Police detained 10 people holding posters critical of Bidzina Ivanishvili.
27 Jul — Tbilisi: Activist Nodar Tsitsriashvili was detained for displaying a similar poster, as daily protests reached 608 consecutive days.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect the ruling Georgian Dream government to continue incremental judicial harassment of journalists, comedians and protest figures rather than a single dramatic crackdown, sustaining the daily-protest equilibrium well past its 600-day mark. Watch for EU/US statements or targeted sanctions responses if detentions of media figures continue to escalate in frequency or severity.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 24-27 Jul — Moscow/Yerevan: Russia's Rosselkhoznadzor enforced a ban on Armenian dairy imports effective 27 Jul, affecting products that made up 78.3% of Armenia's dairy exports.
29 Jul — Yerevan: PM Pashinyan stated the Eurasian Economic Union is 'paralyzed and not functioning,' reflecting deepening EAEU-Armenia tensions.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Russia will likely continue expanding sector-by-sector trade restrictions against Armenia as leverage against Yerevan's EU/US pivot. Pashinyan's public EAEU criticism signals growing willingness to accept economic cost for continued Western alignment, likely accelerating Armenian outreach to alternative markets through year-end.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 13 Jul — Shusha: President Aliyev said Azerbaijan is 'unequivocally considering' full withdrawal from the Council of Europe over the 2024 PACE decision revoking Baku's delegation voting rights.
20-21 Jul — Berlin: Aliyev made an official visit to Germany, meeting Steinmeier and Merz, and highlighted new gas supplies to Germany.
Late Jul — Berlin: Aliyev confirmed secret Russia-Germany talks had been held in Baku, positioning Azerbaijan as a diplomatic intermediary.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Azerbaijan will likely continue leveraging its energy relationship with Europe as counterweight to the PACE dispute, using the Council of Europe threat as negotiating pressure rather than following through on withdrawal. Baku's disclosed role hosting Russia-Germany contacts suggests further high-level shuttle diplomacy in Q3-Q4 2026.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Sudan's El Obeid siege has escalated in line with the prior 'next El Fasher' warning but has not yet produced a mass-casualty ground event — RSF drone retaliation intensified immediately after SAF's 27 Jul highway recapture, and RSF units retreating from North Kordofan turned on civilians in reprisal raids, with HRW and UN investigators continuing to warn the trajectory mirrors El Fasher's fall.

Mali's FLA-JNIM alliance has shifted from the dramatic Anefis-Tabankort convoy battle (now confirmed at 50+ FAMa/Africa Corps dead) to a lower-visibility campaign of blockades, infrastructure sabotage and localized clashes, with genuinely little fresh, independently-verified incident reporting this week.

Niger's security emergency is bifurcating into two active fronts — the established Tillabéri JNIM-ISSP battleground is now compounded by a resurgent Boko Haram/ISWAP push into Diffa, evidenced by the 31 Jul N'Guigmi ambush that killed 14 security personnel, stretching Nigerien forces across geographically separated theaters simultaneously.

Nigeria's twin crises intensified without resolution — Zamfara saw a new mass-displacement/abduction event alongside a rescue operation, while in Borno the 36 Lassa students remain largely unaccounted for a month after their abduction despite incremental peripheral rescues, illustrating a broader pattern where tactical security wins are not translating into strategic de-escalation.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 18 Jul — Anefis/Tabankort: A joint JNIM-FLA ambush on a FAMa-Africa Corps convoy killed at least 50 Malian and Africa Corps personnel, per multiple outlets, firming up a casualty figure that was still unconfirmed last week.
26 Jul — Niono area, Ségou region: Africa Corps and FAMa forces clashed with JNIM/FLA fighters, reportedly killing 8 militants (per Russian state-aligned Pravda Mali; unverified independently).
Ongoing — Ségou region: FAMa's 'Operation Dougoukoloko' claimed to have cleared several JNIM/FLA hideouts, while a JNIM fuel and road blockade around Bamako imposed since roughly 10 Jul continued.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. JNIM-FLA is likely to sustain a two-track strategy: continued harassment/ambush operations against FAMa-Africa Corps positions in the north and persistent economic pressure on Bamako via road blockades and infrastructure sabotage. Africa Corps' reluctance to conduct offensive operations after the Anefis losses suggests further consolidation around the capital rather than reassertion of control in the north, with continued risk of a high-casualty urban or peri-urban attack within the quarter.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 17 Jul — Téra, Tillabéri region: 16 Nigerien soldiers were killed and 23 wounded in a militant attack near the tri-border zone.

31 Jul — N'Guigmi, Diffa Region: A coordinated terrorist attack and follow-on ambush killed at least 14 Nigerien Defence and Security Forces personnel near a National Guard position, roughly 1km from a prepared ambush site.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained; broadened framing. Niger is now facing simultaneous pressure on two active fronts rather than one — expect continued high-casualty ambushes in Tillabéri as JNIM and ISSP compete for territorial control, compounded by a resurgent Boko Haram/ISWAP push into Diffa. Nigerien forces, already stretched, are likely to struggle to reinforce both fronts simultaneously, raising the risk of further mass-casualty attacks on isolated garrisons.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 28 Jul — Gorom Gorom, Sahel region: ISSP attacked a Burkinabè military/VDP-escorted humanitarian convoy carrying food and aid to the besieged town, killing at least 9 civilians; witnesses said the convoy carried no weapons.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Reporting genuinely thinned this week relative to late June/early July, when a large multi-town JNIM assault dominated coverage; only one clearly-dated new incident was confirmed. Expect continued targeting of humanitarian access routes and besieged towns (Djibo, Gorom Gorom) by both JNIM and ISSP, with civilians and aid convoys increasingly caught between blockade tactics and military escort failures.

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 27 Jul — El Obeid: RSF drone strikes hit two municipal buildings at dawn, in apparent retaliation hours after SAF regained control of the Khartoum-El Obeid highway.

29 Jul — North Kordofan (Um Badr, Sodari, Abu Zaima, Hamrat al-Sheikh, El Mazroub): RSF units retreating from North Kordofan launched retaliatory attacks on civilians, looting markets and detaining residents accused of aiding SAF.

Through late Jul — El Obeid/North Kordofan: HRW/UN reporting describes 10 consecutive days of drone strikes killing at least 50 civilians, an intensification from the prior week's tally of 45+ over three weeks.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. No mass-casualty ground-assault event has yet occurred in El Obeid, but SAF's highway recapture appears to have triggered an intensified RSF retaliatory drone campaign — a worrying escalation indicator. Given explicit UN/HRW warnings of El Fasher-style atrocity risk, a ground assault on El Obeid within the quarter cannot be ruled out, particularly if RSF consolidates its North Kordofan retreat into a renewed encirclement effort.

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 20-22 Jul — Kalbus/Al-Tina, West Darfur border: SAF, the Joint Force and RSF all reinforced positions near the Chad border; an RSF drone strike on Al-Tina town killed and injured civilians and military personnel, with explosions and airstrikes heard from refugee camps inside Chad.
30 Jul — N'Djamena: Chad and France reported progress rebuilding military relations, a sign N'Djamena is diversifying security partnerships amid the border pressure.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No new dated attack inside Chadian territory itself was confirmed this week, but spillover risk from the Darfur side is rising, with fighting now directly audible and visible from Chadian refugee camps. Expect continued reinforcement of the Chad-Sudan border by all three armed actors, with elevated risk of a direct spillover incident if RSF pushes on Al-Tina.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: 14-18 Jul — Off Nouadhibou: 144 refugees and migrants were confirmed dead or missing across a series of Atlantic-route incidents, confirmed by UNHCR, IOM and MSF as the deadliest 2026 migration-route disaster; no further dated maritime incident was found for the 24-31 Jul window specifically.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No new incident was identified this week — reported as such rather than invented — though this does not indicate reduced structural risk on the Atlantic migration route. Expect continued but lower-visibility departures from Mauritanian and neighboring shores, with elevated risk of further mass-casualty incidents as Q3 weather and current conditions typically worsen, given limited rescue capacity out of Nouadhibou.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 23 Jul — Maru LGA, Zamfara: Bandits sustained attacks over four consecutive days on Tashar Mayanchi and 10+ neighboring communities; at least 20 people killed, 40+ residents abducted.
26 Jul — Magami village, Kaura Namoda LGA, Zamfara: Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma rescued 48 kidnap victims following a bandit attack; 1 civilian killed and 2 injured in the resulting firefight.
27-28 Jul — Borno State: Troops of Operation Hadin Kai foiled a terrorist infiltration attempt and evacuated 21 students; six abductees were separately rescued in Mussa, Askira/Uba LGA.
Ongoing — Lassa, Borno: The 36 students and 1 staff member abducted 29-30 Jun remain largely in captivity a month on, despite a mid-July proof-of-life video.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Both the northwest (Zamfara banditry) and northeast (Borno ISWAP/JAS) theaters remained highly active this week, with the state notching tactical rescues that have not resolved the underlying mass-abduction crisis. Expect continued cyclical bandit raids in Zamfara and persistent ISWAP/JAS infiltration pressure in Borno; the Lassa students are at meaningful risk of remaining in captivity well beyond the 90-day horizon absent a negotiated release or decisive rescue operation.

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: South China Sea friction has plateaued at an elevated baseline rather than continuing to escalate week-on-week — after the 20 and 24 July Second Thomas/Scarborough clashes, no new physical confrontation was confirmed through 31 July, coinciding with a five-day US-Philippines-Japan joint maritime exercise and a US carrier strike group patrol, though the underlying dispute and China's demonstrated willingness to use physical force remain unresolved.

China is running a coordinated two-front gray-zone pressure campaign against Taiwan and the Philippines simultaneously — Taiwan Strait median-line incursions and Fujian live-fire drills were timed directly against Taiwan's Han Kuang exercise, while South China Sea coercion against Manila continued in parallel, indicating a deliberate strategic choice to test multiple flashpoints in the same window.

Political violence emerged as an underappreciated new risk vector this week, distinct from the region's established insurgency/airstrike conflicts — Pakistan's AJK election produced up to 30 deaths in security force-JAAC clashes, and Thailand-Cambodia border fighting resumed with 38+ killed and 300,000 newly displaced before a fresh ceasefire, both sharp deteriorations from 'stable' or 'holding' assessments just one week prior.

Myanmar's airstrike campaign shows no sign of tapering and is broadening geographically, with simultaneous Rakhine/Mandalay/Sagaing/Chin operations within the same week reinforcing its status as the region's most acute civilian-harm crisis, while Indonesia's Papua conflict shows a similar self-reinforcing escalation dynamic between TNI operations and TPNPB-OPM reprisal killings of alleged informants.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 19 Jul (satellite analysis published) — Kaesong vicinity: RFA satellite imagery confirmed roughly 52m-long structures at a North Korean base south of Kaesong, with at least 21 buildings assessed as multiple-rocket-launcher storage/maintenance facilities.
27 Jul — Pyongyang: Kim Yo Jong rejected the ASEAN Regional Forum's renewed call for 'complete denuclearization,' calling it 'stupid' and 'foolish.'
28 Jul — Pyongyang: Kim Jong Un presided over ceremonies marking the 73rd anniversary of the Korean War armistice, reaffirming frontline-unit fortification policy.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect continued incremental militarization of the DMZ corridor near Kaesong alongside a hardened rhetorical posture rejecting any denuclearization framework raised in multilateral fora. A discrete provocation is plausible within 30-60 days, timed to US-ROK exercises or diplomatic milestones, but sustained low-level friction remains more probable than a major crisis absent an external trigger.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 17-20 Jul — Mindat, Chin State: Junta aircraft conducted repeated bombing runs, including 30+ bombs dropped on 20 Jul.
19 Jul — Ma-Ei, Taungup Township, Rakhine: A junta jet dropped three 500-lb bombs, killing 5 civilians and injuring 14, including a monk and three children.
25-26 Jul — Rakhine/Mandalay/Sagaing: A coordinated wave of airstrikes and drone attacks killed at least 6 civilians and injured 26+, destroying 25+ homes and a church.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Airstrike tempo remains undiminished and has broadened geographically, consistent with cumulative reporting of 450+ civilian deaths from mass-casualty incidents in H1 2026. Expect continued indiscriminate use of airstrikes against AA/PDF-held territory through the 90-day window, with civilian infrastructure remaining at elevated risk and no credible de-escalation signal present.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 27-28 Jul — Rawalakot, AJK: Phase-1 AJK polling was marred by deadly clashes between security forces and JAAC supporters marching on Muzaffarabad; 2 security personnel killed and up to 30 protesters reported killed over two days.
27 Jul — AJK-wide: PML-N won 9 of 13 contested Mirpur-division seats in preliminary phase-1 results.
16 Jul — Balochistan: Operation Shaban's toll reached 129 militants killed since 5 Jul.
31 Jul — AJK-wide: The campaign period closed ahead of phase-2 polling (2 Aug, 21 constituencies, 1.7 million+ eligible voters).
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The AJK election-violence death toll marks a significant new escalation vector distinct from the Balochistan counter-terror campaign, indicating JAAC-security force friction has crossed into lethal confrontation for the first time this cycle. Expect heightened security lockdown ahead of and during phase-2 (2 Aug) and phase-3 (10 Aug) polling, with continued risk of further clashes, while Operation Shaban continues grinding through August without a clear end-state.

countries.name: India
incidents: 21 Jul — Chandel district, Manipur: Security forces arrested 3 KYKL cadres near the Indo-Myanmar border.
21 Jul — Ukhrul district, Manipur: Security forces destroyed 2 illegal insurgent bunkers.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Manipur counter-insurgency operations continue at a steady tempo along the porous Indo-Myanmar border corridor, with periodic KYKL arrests and bunker destruction. No indicators of a broadening conflict or major flare-up were found for this period.

countries.name: China
incidents: 20-21 Jul — Taiwan Strait (R9 restricted zone): A PLA helicopter and UAV crossed the median line together and lingered east of it for roughly 9.5 hours, the first extended-duration median-line loiter by a PLA helicopter.
23-24 Jul — Waters off Dongshan Island, Fujian: The PLA conducted two consecutive days of live-fire drills, timed against Taiwan's Han Kuang exercise.
20 Jul — Second Thomas Shoal: Chinese Coast Guard personnel rammed and physically clashed with Philippine Navy craft, injuring a service member.
24 Jul — Scarborough Shoal: China Coast Guard used water cannon and blocking maneuvers against Philippine resupply vessels.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Beijing is layering simultaneous gray-zone pressure on two fronts — sustained median-line normalization near Taiwan and physical coercion against the Philippines — timed to Taiwan's Han Kuang exercise. Expect continued incremental median-line crossings and further live-fire drills timed to Taiwanese political statements, alongside a persistent but lower-frequency baseline of South China Sea friction.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 9-29 Jul — Islandwide: The Han Kuang 41 exercise, the largest and longest in the program's history, ran its full 10-day course rehearsing invasion-response scenarios.
20-21 Jul — Taiwan Strait: PLA helicopter/UAV median-line crossing and extended loiter in the R9 restricted zone drew a direct Taiwanese MND response.
24 Jul — Keelung: Prosecutors detained an Nvidia employee, expanding the AI-chip smuggling probe to 7 suspects; roughly 50 servers worth NT$700M were seized.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The chip-smuggling investigation is escalating in scale and international scope, with further arrests likely as the multi-jurisdictional probe matures. Militarily, expect the PLA to sustain or increase gray-zone pressure in the immediate aftermath of Han Kuang, testing Taiwan's post-exercise readiness posture, with incremental normalization of median-line crossings anticipated as a persistent baseline.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 20 Jul — Second Thomas Shoal: China Coast Guard personnel rammed a Philippine inflatable craft and exchanged blows with batons/oars, injuring a service member; US Secretary of State Rubio issued a formal condemnation.
21-25 Jul — South China Sea: The Philippines conducted the 17th Multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity, a five-day joint exercise with the US and Japan.
24 Jul — Scarborough Shoal: China Coast Guard used water cannon and blocking maneuvers to prevent a Philippine fishermen resupply mission.
27 Jul — South China Sea: A US Navy carrier strike group was reported patrolling the contested waters, signaling sustained US presence beyond the joint drills.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Direct physical confrontation frequency appears to have plateaued after the 20-24 July clashes, likely reflecting the deterrent effect of the concurrent joint exercise and continued US carrier presence. The underlying dispute remains unresolved and China's willingness to use physical force has now been demonstrated repeatedly, lowering the threshold for recurrence; expect intermittent flare-ups tied to Philippine resupply missions.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: Late Jul — Nationwide: A new Kimsuky (APT43) campaign was confirmed compromising South Korean groupware/collaboration-software vendors as an intermediary vector to reach downstream defense and institutional customers, using a mail-server exploit and Gomir-variant malware.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Kimsuky/APT43 has shifted tactics toward supply-chain compromise of software vendors rather than direct targeting, indicating a maturing and harder-to-detect intrusion methodology. Expect continued disclosure of downstream victims as the vendor-compromise investigation unfolds, with likely additional advisories from South Korean cybersecurity authorities.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 11 Jul — International: 14 countries issued a joint statement marking the 10th anniversary of the 2016 Hague Tribunal ruling against China's South China Sea claims; Vietnam notably did not co-sign, continuing its bilateral-management approach.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; sparse new reporting this window. Vietnam likely continues its established pattern of quiet bilateral hedging — deepening defense ties with the Philippines while avoiding multilateral statements that could provoke direct confrontation with Beijing.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 19 Jul — Tokyo: Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi stated Japan 'cannot avoid' a national debate on nuclear weapons ahead of a year-end review of key security documents.
21-23 Jul — Tokyo: Koizumi's remarks drew sustained coverage, citing Finland's parliamentary authorization of nuclear weapons basing and France's warhead expansion as comparative justifications.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, watch for upgrade. This is a significant political escalation rather than a kinetic one — a sitting Defense Minister openly inviting a nuclear-weapons debate is unprecedented for postwar Japan. Expect continued domestic political maneuvering around the security-document revision process, though an actual policy shift remains unlikely within the 90-day window.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 17 Jul — KM 4 Logpon area, Dekai District, Yahukimo: Indonesian security forces killed 3 TPNPB-OPM members in an operation.
20-21 Jul — Seradala District, Yahukimo: TPNPB-OPM claimed responsibility for executing 3 civilians accused of acting as informants for TNI operations.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The Yahukimo killings reflect an escalating cycle of TPNPB-OPM targeting of perceived collaborators alongside TNI's continued militarization of the Trans Papua corridor. Expect continued tit-for-tat violence — TNI/police operations against TPNPB-OPM cells alternating with reprisal killings of alleged informants — with limited prospect of de-escalation absent a political dialogue track.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 24 Jul — Thai-Cambodia border (6+ locations): Deadly fighting erupted, killing at least 38 and wounding 200 by 28 Jul, with roughly 300,000 newly displaced on both sides.
28 Jul — Kuala Lumpur (mediated by PM Anwar Ibrahim): Thai Acting PM Phumtham and Cambodian PM Hun Manet agreed to a new unconditional ceasefire.
29 Jul — Border areas: The Thai army accused Cambodia of violating the new ceasefire; Cambodia denied the allegation.
31 Jul — Border areas: UN reporting confirms 20,000+ Cambodians remain displaced and border crossings remain closed.
countries.coa: Upgraded to MODERATE from LOW. This represents a significant deterioration from the prior 'ceasefire holding' assessment — active fighting resumed on 24 July with substantial casualties and mass new displacement before a fresh ceasefire was brokered on 28 July, followed immediately by mutual violation accusations. Expect intermittent border skirmishes to continue testing the new ceasefire through the 90-day window, with displacement figures unlikely to improve meaningfully given closed crossings.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: 22 Jul — Dhaka: The BNP publicly distanced itself from the July National Charter-backed reform agenda, favoring its own 31-point reform outline.

22 Jul — Dhaka: Jamaat-e-Islami and the NCP criticized BNP's refusal to take the oath as members of the Constitutional Reform Council, framing it as contradicting the spirit of the 2024 July Uprising.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The BNP-NCP/Jamaat rift has hardened into an explicit public divergence over implementation mechanics, raising the risk of a genuine constitutional impasse ahead of the national election. Expect continued political friction and possible parliamentary gridlock, though outright unrest is not yet indicated.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: 5-6 Jul — Negombo Prison: The Human Rights Commission confirmed the prison violence left at least 28 dead, including 7 prison officials, a more precise figure than the prior 25-28 estimate.
7-8 Jul — Welikada Prison: HRCSL officers were initially denied access during an unannounced inspection visit; access was granted the following day.
Ongoing — Multiple prisons: HRCSL is investigating allegations of torture of inmates transferred from Negombo and the deaths of two inmates in custody.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The HRCSL investigation is expanding in scope beyond the initial Negombo incident to include transfer-related torture allegations and in-custody deaths at receiving prisons, with international pressure building for accountability. Risk of further unrest at overcrowded facilities receiving transferred inmates remains elevated.

regions.name: Americas
overview: Colombia's inauguration venue crisis has resolved procedurally but not politically — Congress ratified Cali's Arena USC after a last-minute volcanic-activity scare forced abandonment of the Cauca option, but Petro's confirmed boycott over unsubstantiated fraud claims means Colombia inaugurates its next president outside Bogotá for the first time in modern history amid heavy security and an unresolved legitimacy dispute.

Cuba's blackout-driven protest wave has outlasted its most symbolically dangerous test — cacerolazo demonstrations recurred in Havana, Santiago and Cienfuegos even after tactical power restorations around the 26 July Revolution Day anniversary, while Havana's messaging has pivoted to blaming Washington rather than addressing the underlying grid collapse.

Venezuela's post-Maduro governance remains internationally contested and legally ambiguous — Acting President Delcy Rodríguez faces a formal UN fact-finding mission rebuke over the ICC withdrawal even as Washington calibrates open-ended support for her, while earthquake recovery and continuing opposition/Chavista mobilization keep the domestic environment fluid heading into a National Assembly mandate decision.

Elsewhere, modest stabilization is visible but fragile — Bolivia's $1.9bn IMF deal and Peru's completed transition to Fujimori offer positive signals, yet a fresh arrest order against Evo Morales could re-ignite Bolivia's paused blockade movement, while Haiti's under-strength Gang Suppression Force remains unable to reverse gangs' 85% control of Port-au-Prince and is now requesting a mandate extension through 2028.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 28 Jul — Caracas: Machado-aligned opposition supporters marched demanding release of political prisoner Gabriel Barros, while a simultaneous Chavista counter-mobilization denounced perceived US influence.

29 Jul — Geneva: The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela publicly urged Caracas to reverse its Rome Statute/ICC withdrawal, warning it would weaken accountability for alleged crimes against humanity.

30 Jul — International: President Trump publicly stated Acting President Delcy Rodríguez 'has to say' Maduro remains the legitimate president, underscoring continued ambiguity over the legal basis and duration of her caretaker mandate.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. No single decisive event, but converging pressure points — the 28 Jul dueling mobilizations, the ICC withdrawal dispute, and continued earthquake humanitarian strain — sustain elevated risk. Expect Rodríguez's caretaker authority to remain internationally contested but functionally unchallenged domestically, with the National Assembly's window to extend her mandate becoming a near-term flashpoint. Opposition mobilization under Machado will likely continue at low intensity around prisoner-release demands rather than escalate into mass unrest.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 20 Jul — New York (UNSC): GSF Special Representative Jack Christofides briefed the Security Council, presenting the force's first detailed operational roadmap and formally requesting a mandate extension through September 2028.

Ongoing — Port-au-Prince: The GSF remains at roughly 1,000 of 5,550 authorized personnel, continuing patrols and gang-barricade clearance; full operational capacity is not expected until October 2026.
Ongoing — Port-au-Prince/Artibonite/Centre: Gangs control an estimated 85% of the Port-au-Prince metro area and are expanding into Artibonite, Centre and the Kenscoff highlands.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The GSF will likely remain understrength through the reporting period, reaching only partial operational capacity by October, meaning no material reduction in gang territorial control is expected before year-end. The mandate-extension request through September 2028 signals the mission itself now expects a multi-year, not near-term, resolution; displacement pressure into Artibonite, Centre and Kenscoff suggests gang expansion beyond the capital will continue.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 28 Jul — Bogotá: The House of Representatives voted 117-7 to relocate the 7 Aug presidential inauguration to Cali's Arena USC, after the Senate's earlier approval of Popayán (Cauca) was abandoned over volcanic activity risk near the Puracé Volcano.
29 Jul — Bogotá: The Senate ratified the Cali venue 58-30, the first Colombian presidential inauguration held outside Bogotá in modern history.
29 Jul — Cali: A special security plan was announced for 7 Aug, including a Unified Command Post, added troop deployments and access controls around Arena USC.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The procedural venue fight is resolved, but the underlying legitimacy dispute is not — Petro remains firm he will boycott the ceremony over unproven fraud allegations dismissed by the Registry, Electoral Council and Inspector General. Expect the 7 Aug inauguration to proceed in Cali under heavy security with no violent disruption of the ceremony itself, though the fraud narrative will likely persist as a legitimacy irritant. ELN/Clan del Golfo violence in Chocó continues unabated, insulated from Bogotá's political turmoil.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 24 Jul — Havana/Santiago de Cuba/Cienfuegos: The Assembly of Cuban Resistance called for coordinated pot-banging protests ahead of the politically sensitive 26 Jul Revolution Day anniversary; cacerolazo protests occurred despite pre-emptive power restorations in some neighborhoods.
26 Jul — Nationwide: Grid deficit exceeded 2,200 MW on Revolution Day itself, with outages affecting all provinces amid fuel-oil and diesel reserves fully exhausted since May.
30 Jul — Havana: President Díaz-Canel dismissed a 20 Jul US State Department report on Cuba as a 'propaganda pamphlet,' redirecting blame for blackout-driven unrest onto Washington.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, now the largest sustained protest wave since July 2021 and still spreading geographically. The regime's tactic of selectively restoring power to defuse planned protest dates has proven only partially effective; expect continued near-daily localized cacerolazos through August as fuel shortages persist, with Díaz-Canel's rhetorical strategy of externalizing blame onto the US likely to continue rather than pivot toward infrastructure fixes.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 21 Jul — Manabí (Manta, San Mateo)/San Martín: Human Rights Watch published 'A Dangerous Partnership,' documenting abuses in joint US-Ecuador counter-narcotics operations, including a March 2026 incident where soldiers detained and tortured four men with electric shocks and water-boarding-style methods.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained; no confirmed new Manabí gang-violence incident was found dated specifically within this window, reported as a gap rather than an absence of risk. The HRW findings add a reputational and legal-accountability dimension to the ongoing militarized campaign, which remains locked in through 2029, and may generate diplomatic friction in Washington but is unlikely to alter Noboa's security posture near-term.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 28 Jul — Lima: Keiko Fujimori was formally inaugurated as President, pledging an 'iron fist' security policy including five CECOT-style mega-prisons, anonymous judges for criminal trials and mandatory prison labor.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The transition proceeded without major disruption, but the extortion and sicariato crisis driving her mandate remains unresolved, with her security agenda not yet implemented — the mega-prison program will take considerably longer than 90 days to materialize. Expect continued transport-sector killings and extortion-linked violence in Lima/Callao at or near the current pace through the transition period.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 29 Jul — La Paz/Washington: The IMF and Bolivia reached agreement on a $1.9 billion financing program, pending IMF executive board approval, expected to unlock over $5 billion combined with World Bank/IDB support.

30 Jul — Santa Cruz: Departmental prosecutors issued an arrest order against former president Evo Morales over his alleged role in organizing the May-June road blockades, on six charges including armed uprising and terrorism.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, mixed signals. The IMF program is a stabilizing development that should ease near-term FX and reserve pressure. The Morales arrest order is a watch item: his rural/Indigenous support base had only paused, not abandoned, its protest campaign in late June, and its response over coming weeks will determine whether unrest reignites.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 30 Jul — Santo Domingo: Migration authorities reported the 2026 deportation campaign has cost RD$5 billion so far, with 226,000 Haitians deported year-to-date, continuing routine weekly operations.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. No new violent security incident was found this window; the deportation campaign continues at or near its established pace, sustained by officials' own acknowledgment of a 'revolving door' dynamic of repeated re-crossings.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 21 Jul — Kingston: Police fatal shootings continued their decline — 8 killed by security forces in July through the 21st, down from 20 in June, for 167 cumulative year-to-date.
30 Jul — Harbour View, Kingston: One man was killed and a firearm seized in a police shootout.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Both murders and police-involved fatalities are trending favorably, though isolated violent incidents continue; officials caution against complacency. Community-protest risk over police lethality remains latent but not currently active.
